title: Iran Human Rights Monitor Documents 61 Executions in 24 Days — One Every 9.6 Hours
detail: Iran Human Rights Monitor documented 61 executions across prisons nationwide — from Tabriz to Zahedan — between August 23 and September 15, 2026, a pace of roughly 2.5 per day, or one every 9.6 hours. The report names victims including Mohammadreza Majidi-Asl, 34, arrested during the December 2025–January 2026 protests and executed after the Supreme Court rejected his appeal on a charge of 'operational action for a hostile state,' and Omidreza Heidari, a 19-year-old student from Izeh sentenced by the Isfahan Revolutionary Court amid reports of torture during interrogation. The report ties the executions to a broader pattern of evidence destruction at detention and mass-grave sites, including the demolition of Gohardasht Prison in Karaj that began September 13.

media.caption: Iran Human Rights Monitor documents 61 executions over a 24-day period

confidenceReason: Reported by an opposition-aligned Iranian diaspora human rights monitor; not independently corroborated by wire services given restricted access to Iranian prisons.

title: Amnesty International: Iran Committed Crimes Against Humanity Crushing 2022 Protests, Warns 2026 Crackdown Is Worse
detail: Amnesty International released a nearly 1,000-page report concluding that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity — including murder, torture, rape and enforced disappearance — in crushing the 2022 'Woman, Life, Freedom' protests that followed Mahsa Amini's death. The report identifies 377 protesters and bystanders killed, including 56 children, and names 87 national and regional officials in the chain of command it holds responsible. Amnesty said the state's suppression of new 2025–2026 protests bears the 'same hallmarks' as 2022 but on 'an even deadlier and more staggering scale.' Secretary General Agnès Callamard said: 'The extensive evidence gathered and analyzed in our report leaves no doubt: Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity to crush the 2022 Woman Life Freedom uprising.' Amnesty urged the UN General Assembly to create an international criminal justice mechanism to prosecute those most responsible.

media.caption: Amnesty International report documents crimes against humanity in Iran's crackdown on the 2022 protests
